samples.summary: Only `..` is tested against DOT_SEGMENT; the single-dot `.` case and the `%2e` alternatives of the regex are never exercised
samples.evidence: DOT_SEGMENT is `/^(?:\.|%2e){1,2}$/i`, covering `.`, `..`, `%2e`, `%2e%2e`, `.%2e`, `%2e.`. Every new test (http-client-paths.test.ts:132-159, read-dry-run.test.ts:299-320) passes only `..`. A single `.` id — which the URL parser also resolves away — is never asserted to be refused, so a regex regression to `/^\.\.$/` would keep the whole suite green. The `%2e` alternatives are in fact unreachable because `seg` tests the *encoded* value and `encodeURIComponent` escapes `%` to `%25` (the test at line 161-171 documents exactly that), so those branches are both untested and untestable — nothing pins whether they are intentional dead code.

verdict.reason: The empty-segment branch in seg() (url.ts:33, distinct from the DOT_SEGMENT branch) is genuinely untested. The new suites cover only `..`: http-client-paths.test.ts:131-178 and read-dry-run.test.ts:300-322. No test file imports client/url directly (grep 'client/url' matches only src/** importers); repo-wide grep for 'Invalid identifier' matches only src files, those two test files, docs/design/cli.md and .agent-review artifacts; grep for `workspace: ''`/`""` in tests returns nothing; grep for empty-string arguments in packages/cli/test yields only join('')/parse*Format('')/measureWidth(''), none reaching seg(). The only end-to-end commander-driven suite (output.test.ts:210-308) pins WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE='ws-1', and bin.test.ts stubs runCli entirely. The premise also holds: resolveConfig defaults workspace to '' in all four branches (config.ts:96-100,121-126,143-147,160-164), so the empty branch is the one most likely to fire in ordinary unconfigured use, and config.ts:108 / config.test.ts:99-103 still document the superseded `/workspaces//...` 404 behaviour. A behavior change plus a new user-facing error message with no meaningful test = major under the missing-tests rule.

finding.summary: The workspace-segment encoding — the change's own headline attacker-reachable input — has no test
finding.evidence: Both new suites hardcode a benign workspace: `workspace: 'ws-1'` (http-client-paths.test.ts:17) and `const WORKSPACE = 'ws-1'` (read-dry-run.test.ts:46). The diff adds `seg(this.config.workspace)` in three separate places (`HttpClient.base`, the three api-key URL builders, `printDryRun`, and `apiKeysUrl` in commands/api-keys.ts) and its own doc comment argues `config.workspace` "is as attacker-reachable as the rest (`--workspace`, `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`, or a profile in the YAML config)". Yet `ws-1` encodes to itself, so every one of those `seg()` calls could be deleted and the whole suite would still be green. I grepped `packages/cli/test` for `workspace` (all matches are `ws-1`/`ws-flag`/`wid` style literals) and read both new test files; no case passes a `../` or `?` workspace.

verdict.reason: The claimed gap does not exist. http-client-paths.test.ts contains a dedicated `describe('the workspace segment')` block (lines 88-121) built on `const HOSTILE: CliConfig = { ...CONFIG, workspace: '../../admin/users' }` (line 89), with three tests asserting the percent-encoded workspace on the v1 API base (lines 94-99), the api-key management route (lines 105-107) and the multipart files route (lines 117-119) — plus line 154-159 asserting a bare `..` workspace is refused before any request is built. Deleting `seg(this.config.workspace)` would make every one of these fail (raw `../../admin/users` != `..%2F..%2Fadmin%2Fusers`, and the `new URL(...).pathname` assertion at line 97 would see the traversal resolved). Independently, read-dry-run.test.ts covers the preview path: its `run()` helper threads a workspace through the real `--workspace` flag (lines 51-66) and two tests pass `'../../admin'`, asserting `.../api/v1/workspaces/..%2F..%2Fadmin/documents/doc-1` (line 287) and `.../workspaces/..%2F..%2Fadmin/api-keys` (line 296), exercising `apiV1Base`/`apiKeysUrl` in src/client/url.ts:50,61 for real (only HttpClient's methods are mocked, and the tests assert those mocks were not called). The reviewer's grep for 'workspace' in packages/cli/test evidently missed these blocks; the finding's premise is factually wrong.
